These ten hypotheses come from what is generally known about NAS-Bench-201, not from data: none of the 100 experiments have been run. I expect three regularities to drive most of the interactions:

- **Filling an empty slot helps more.** An edit that puts an operation on an edge currently set to `none` usually gains more than one that swaps out an existing useful operation.
- **Losing the last path hurts most.** Removing or weakening an edge costs much more when the cell has few other routes from input to output.
- **The 0→3 skip connection matters most when convs are deep.** It is the most valuable edge in cells built from stacked 3x3 convolutions.
